outlooks.summary: SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ARE EXPECTED ACROSS MUCH OF THE NORTHERN AND CENTRAL PLAINS INTO THE UPPER MISSISSIPPI VALLEY...AND THROUGH THE MIDWEST AND SOUTHERN GREAT LAKES EASTWARD INTO PENNSYLVANIA. ISOLATED SEVERE STORMS ARE ALSO POSSIBLE FROM CENTRAL KANSAS INTO WEST TEXAS. LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE THE MAIN THREATS...WITH THE MOST SIGNIFICANT SEVERE STORMS EXPECTED ACROSS THE DAKOTAS AND MINNESOTA.

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: CLOSED LOW CENTERED OVER ERN ID/WRN MT PER WATER VAPOR IMAGERY IS EXPECTED TO BECOME MORE PROGRESSIVE THIS FORECAST PERIOD AS IT MOVES NNE TOWARD THE NRN MT BORDER NEAR SRN ALBERTA AND SWRN SASKATCHEWAN. AS THIS OCCURS...A MIDLEVEL IMPULSE IS EXPECTED TO TRACK NEWD INTO THE DAKOTAS THIS AFTERNOON. A STRONGER SHORTWAVE TROUGH...NOW MOVING EWD THROUGH NV...WILL REACH THE CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS BY 19/00Z AND THEN TRACK ACROSS NEB TO THE ERN DAKOTAS/WRN MN BY 12Z THU. MEANWHILE...A COMPACT SHORTWAVE TROUGH WILL TRACK ESEWD FROM WI/LOWER MI REGION AND WEAKEN AS IT REACHES NY WITHIN THE BASE OF TROUGH IN THE NORTHEAST STATES. WEAKER IMPULSES ARE EXPECTED TO TRACK ESEWD THROUGH THE MIDWEST...OH VALLEY TO PA REGION. AT THE SURFACE...AN AREA OF LOW PRESSURE WILL MOVE SLOWLY NORTH TOWARD SRN ALBERTA...WHILE A SECOND LOW TRACKS NEWD INTO CENTRAL SD THIS AFTERNOON AND THEN INTO ERN SD BY LATE AFTERNOON/EARLY EVENING. A WARM FRONT ADVANCING NEWD ACROSS THE DAKOTAS WILL BE A FOCUS FOR TSTMS THROUGH MUCH OF THE FORECAST PERIOD. MEANWHILE...THE ERN EXTENT OF THIS BOUNDARY CURRENTLY EXTENDING FROM FAR SRN MN THROUGH SRN WI...SRN LOWER MI AND REMNANT CONVECTIVE OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES WILL EACH FOCUS NEW TS

sections.title: ND/SD/NEB TO UPPER MS VALLEY
sections.text: A VERY MOIST AND VERY UNSTABLE ENVIRONMENT RESIDING OVER IA/ERN NEB WILL ADVECT NWWD INTO THE DAKOTAS AS SELY LOW LEVEL WINDS STRENGTHEN THROUGH THE DAY FROM IA/WRN MN INTO THE CENTRAL DAKOTAS. SURFACE HEATING MAY BE SOMEWHAT LIMITED INITIALLY ACROSS NRN SD AND ND DUE TO CLOUD DEBRIS FROM CONVECTION PRECEDING THE START OF DAY 1. HOWEVER...THE ABUNDANT MOISTURE RETURN BENEATH A PLUME OF STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES AND EVEN SOME SURFACE HEATING SHOULD RESULT IN A MODERATE TO VERY UNSTABLE AIR MASS INVOF THE WARM FRONT IN THE DAKOTAS. THIS COMBINED WITH EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR OF 35-45 KT WILL SUPPORT ORGANIZED STORMS POTENTIALLY DEVELOPING BY LATE MORNING AND THEN THROUGH THE AFTERNOON AS ASCENT WITH THE LEAD IMPULSE MOVES ACROSS THIS REGION. ALL SEVERE HAZARDS WILL BE POSSIBLE INCLUDING A FEW TORNADOES AND VERY LARGE HAIL. A STRENGTHENING SLY LLJ EXTENDING FROM THE CENTRAL PLAINS INTO THE ERN DAKOTAS AND MN THIS EVENING THROUGH TONIGHT COMBINED WITH VERY STRONG TO EXTREME INSTABILITY RESIDING OVER THE MID MO VALLEY INTO ERN SD/SRN MN WILL PROMOTE UPSCALE GROWTH OF TSTMS INTO ONE OR MORE MCS/S ADVANCING EWD. THESE MCS/S SHOULD TRACK FROM THE DAKOTAS INTO THE UPPER MS VALLEY WITH DAMAGING

sections.title: MIDWEST/SRN GREAT LAKES AND OH VALLEY TO PA/NRN MD
sections.text: ONE OR MORE MCS/S SHOULD BE ONGOING AT 12Z FROM PARTS OF THE UPPER MS VALLEY INTO THE GREAT LAKES. A VERY MOIST AND MODERATE-VERY STRONG INSTABILITY IS EXPECTED THROUGH THIS CORRIDOR TODAY. EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR OF 30-40 KT ORIENTED PARALLEL TO THE SYNOPTIC BOUNDARY AND REMNANT OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES SUGGEST LINE SEGMENTS/BOWS WILL BE POSSIBLE...AS WELL AS A THREAT FOR HAIL.

sections.title: WRN KS SWD THROUGH OK/TX PANHANDLES AND WEST/SOUTHWEST TX
sections.text: MODERATE TO VERY STRONG INSTABILITY IS EXPECTED INVOF THE DRY LINE EXTENDING SWD FROM WRN KS THROUGH THE OK/TX PANHANDLES...WEST TX TO THE TX BIG BEND REGION. THIS COMBINED WITH PW VALUES INCREASING TO 1.25-1.5 INCHES AND STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES WILL SUPPORT MODERATE TO VERY STRONG INSTABILITY THIS AFTERNOON. EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR SHOULD GENERALLY RANGE FROM 30-40 KT...THOUGH VALUES UP TO 45 KT WILL BE POSSIBLE FROM THE TX PANHANDLE INTO WEST TX. ASCENT ALONG THE DRY LINE AND A MIDLEVEL IMPULSE MOVING ACROSS THIS REGION DURING PEAK HEATING SUGGEST TSTMS SHOULD DEVELOP FORM WRN KS SWD THROUGH WEST AND SOUTHWEST TX. VERY LARGE HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH SOME OF THE STORMS IN ADDITION TO A THREAT FOR DAMAGING WIND GUSTS. ..PETERS/SMITH.. 06/18/2014

outlooks.summary: SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ARE EXPECTED OVER MUCH OF THE NORTHERN AND CENTRAL PLAINS AND UPPER MISSISSIPPI VALLEY...AND FROM THE MID-MISSISSIPPI VALLEY AND SOUTHERN GREAT LAKES EASTWARD INTO THE MID-ATLANTIC STATES. MORE ISOLATED SEVERE STORMS MAY OCCUR FROM WESTERN AND CENTRAL KANSAS SOUTHWARD INTO WEST TEXAS. LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE THE MAIN THREATS...BUT TORNADOES ALSO MAY OCCUR...ESPECIALLY OVER PARTS OF SOUTH DAKOTA...NEBRASKA...IOWA...AND MINNESOTA.

sections.title: SYNOPTIC SETUP
sections.text: ID/MT UPR LOW SHOULD EDGE N INTO SE AB BY THE END OF THE PERIOD AS FAIRLY STRONG NE PACIFIC SHORTWAVE TROUGH CONTINUES E TOWARD THE WA/ORE CST. TROUGH EXTENDING S FROM THE ID/MT LOW SHOULD ACCELERATE NNE INTO CNTRL WY BY THIS EVE AND INTO WRN ND EARLY THU AS DOWNSTREAM RIDGE BUILDS N ACROSS THE UPR MS VLY/UPR GRT LKS. FARTHER E...MODERATE W TO NW FLOW WILL PREVAIL OVER THE LWR GRT LKS AND NORTHEAST...ON SRN FRINGE OF QUE UPR LOW. QUASI-STNRY SFC LOW OF RECENT DAYS...NOW CENTERED OVER W CNTRL NEB...SHOULD LIFT SLOWLY NE INTO ERN SD LATER TODAY AND INTO SE ND EARLY THU...WITH A WEAK TROUGH PERSISTING NWWD INTO ERN MT/WRN ND AND LEE TROUGH LINGERING OVER THE CNTRL AND SRN HIGH PLNS. THE ERN PART OF FRONTAL ZONE EXTENDING GENERALLY E FROM THE NEB LOW INTO THE LWR GRT LKS SHOULD SETTLE SWD TODAY AS A SFC RIDGE BUILDS S FROM HUDSON BAY INTO THE NRN GRT LKS. CONVECTIVE OUTFLOW SHOULD TEMPER NWD MOVEMENT OF THE SAME BOUNDARY OVER THE IA/NEB/SD AREA...DESPITE PERSISTENT LOW-LVL WAA ACROSS THE REGION.

sections.title: ND/SD/NEB/MID MO VLY ESE INTO IA THIS AFTN/TNGT
sections.text: RESERVOIR OF VERY STRONG POTENTIAL INSTABILITY...WITH SBCAPE TO 5000 J/KG...WILL PERSIST TODAY ALONG WRN AND SRN FRINGE OF LOW-LVL OUTFLOW ASSOCIATED WITH EXPANSIVE MID-MS VLY/MI MCS. UPR WINDS WILL FURTHER BACK AND SOMEWHAT DECREASE DOWNSTREAM FROM PROGRESSIVE ID/MT UPR LOW. BUT APPRECIABLE LOW-LVL DIRECTIONAL SHEAR WILL LINGER AMIDST RICH LOW-LVL MOISTURE /PW 1.50-1.75 INCHES/ OVER ERN SD S AND SEWD INTO PARTS OF NEB...IA AND SW MN INVOF STALLED OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES. SFC HEATING AND POSSIBLY WEAK UPR DIFFLUENCE SHOULD ONCE AGAIN FOSTER DEVELOPMENT OF WDLY SCTD AFTN/EVE STORMS/SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF TORNADOES...IN ADDITION TO VERY LARGE HAIL AND LOCALLY DMGG WIND. THESE STORMS SHOULD MERGE INTO AN ESE OR SE-MOVING MCS TNGT...EXTENDING A RISK FOR SVR WIND AND POSSIBLY HAIL FARTHER E/SE INTO PARTS OF MN AND IA EARLY THU. FARTHER N...CONSIDERABLY WEAKER BUOYANCY WILL EXIST IN ND RELATIVE TO POINTS S. HOWEVER...MORE SUBSTANTIAL DEEP SHEAR WILL BE PRESENT ON ERN PERIPHERY OF ID-MT UPR LOW. WHILE CLOUDS WILL LIMIT SFC HEATING...FORCING FOR ASCENT E OF THE LOW AND PRESENCE OF EXISTING STORMS MOVING EWD FROM MT SUGGEST A CONDITIONAL RISK FOR SVR HAIL...WIND...AND POSSIBLY A COUPLE TORNADOES

sections.title: CNTRL/SRN PLNS
sections.text: AN UPR IMPULSE NOW OVER ERN NM WILL CONTINUE NNE INTO WRN KS/CNTRL NEB LATER TODAY/TNGT. THIS FEATURE...IN CONJUNCTION WITH LOW-LVL UPLIFT ALONG LEE TROUGH/DRY LINE...MAY SUPPORT DEVELOPMENT OF SCTD SVR STORMS/SUPERCELLS WITH LARGE HAIL AND LOCALLY DMGG WIND FROM W TX NNE INTO SRN NEB. OTHER STORMS WITH A MORE LIMITED RISK FOR SVR HAIL/WIND MAY ARISE LATE IN THE DAY OR THIS EVE OVER NE CO/SW NEB AND NW KS...IN ZONE OF MOIST UPSLOPE FLOW ASSOCIATED WITH PASSAGE OF WEAK FRONTAL SURGE ACROSS REGION. THE NEB AND KS STORMS COULD MERGE INTO A SMALL MCS THAT CONTINUES NEWD ACROSS CNTRL AND ERN NEB TNGT/EARLY THU.

sections.title: MID MS/OH VLYS/SRN LWR MI TO MID ATLANTIC THIS AFTN/EVE
sections.text: MODERATE /25-30 KT/ UNIDIRECTIONAL WLY MID-LVL FLOW WILL PREVAIL FROM SRN WI/IL ESE INTO THE OH VLY/MID ATLANTIC TODAY...ON SW FRINGE OF QUE UPR LOW. MODERATE TO STRONG SFC HEATING SHOULD OCCUR OVER THIS CORRIDOR TODAY...S OF EXPANSIVE BUT WEAKLY ORGANIZED MCS EXTENDING FROM WI INTO LWR MI. LARGE-SCALE FORCING FOR ASCENT WILL BE WEAK...BUT MAY BE AUGMENTED BY APPARENT MCV NOW IN WI...AND BY GLANCING INFLUENCE OF A DISTURBANCE NOW MOVING ESEWD S OF JAMES BAY. COUPLED WITH HIGH PW /AROUND 1.75 INCHES/...SETUP MAY SUPPORT REJUVENATION OF EXISTING STORMS NOW OVER SRN WI...NRN IL...AND SRN LWR MI...AND ADDITIONAL DEVELOPMENT ESEWD INTO PARTS OF IND...OH...AND PA. OTHER STORMS MAY FORM FARTHER ESE OVER THE HIGHER TERRAIN OF SRN PA/WRN MD/WV. WITH SBCAPE OF 2000-2500 J/KG...THE CONVECTION MAY ORGANIZE INTO BROKEN LINES...WITH EMBEDDED SMALL BOWS/PRECIP-ENHANCED DOWNDRAFTS CAPABLE OF DMGG WIND AND MARGINALLY SVR HAIL THROUGH THIS EVE. ..CORFIDI/MARSH.. 06/18/2014

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: A MID TO UPPER-LEVEL LOW AND ASSOCIATED TROUGH FROM THE NRN INTER-MOUNTAIN REGION TO SWRN DESERTS WILL ASSUME AN INCREASING NEGATIVE TILT IN RESPONSE TO THE PROGRESSION OF A POTENT VORTICITY MAXIMUM FROM THE GREAT BASIN INTO NRN HIGH PLAINS. DOWNSTREAM FROM THESE DEVELOPMENTS...A SERIES OF VORTICITY MAXIMA WILL PROGRESS SEWD AROUND AN UPPER LOW CENTERED OVER FAR NERN CANADA...ENHANCING MIDLEVEL FLOW AND FORCING FOR ASCENT ACROSS THE NERN U.S. AT THE SURFACE...AN AREA OF LOW PRESSURE OVER CNTRL NEB WILL DEVELOP NEWD INTO NERN SD/SERN ND BY 19/12Z...WHILE AN ASSOCIATED COLD FRONT ADVANCES EWD THROUGH THE DAKOTAS...AND SEWD THROUGH THE CNTRL HIGH PLAINS. A DRYLINE WILL SHARPEN TODAY FROM THE VICINITY OF THIS LOW PRESSURE SSWWD THROUGH WRN OR CNTRL KS INTO WRN TX. MEANWHILE...A WARM FRONT WHICH HAS BEEN REINFORCED BY CONVECTIVE OUTFLOW WILL ATTEMPT TO MOVE NWD THROUGH PARTS OF THE MID MO VALLEY AND MIDWEST. THE LOCATION OF THIS BOUNDARY WILL LIKELY FLUCTUATE LATITUDINALLY ACROSS THE SRN GREAT LAKES/NRN OH VALLEY OWING TO THE EFFECTS OF CONVECTIVE OUTFLOW. FARTHER E...THIS BOUNDARY WILL SLOWLY SETTLE SWD INTO THE MID ATLANTIC STATES AS A COLD FRONT.

sections.text: THE CO-LOCATION OF A VERY MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER WITH A PRONOUNCED EML WILL ONCE AGAIN YIELD STRONG TO EXTREME INSTABILITY TODAY FROM PARTS OF ERN NEB/WRN IA INTO SERN SD WITH MLCAPE APPROACHING 3000-4500 J/KG. WHERE STRONGER HEATING CAN OCCUR FROM CNTRL SD INTO ND ALONG THE EWD-MOVING COLD FRONT OR INVERTED TROUGH...AFTERNOON MLCAPE MAY RISE INTO THE 1000-2000 J/KG RANGE. OTHER MORE ISOLATED STORMS WILL BE POSSIBLE THIS AFTERNOON INTO EVENING AHEAD OF THE SURFACE LOW AND ALONG THE WARM FRONT OVER SERN SD INTO SWRN MN/NWRN IA. sections.title: CNTRL/SRN PLAINS THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING
sections.text: MORNING WATER VAPOR IMAGERY INDICATES THE PRESENCE OF A WEAK PERTURBATION OVER NM WHICH WILL PRECEDE THE STRONGER GREAT BASIN IMPULSE INTO THE CNTRL/SRN HIGH PLAINS TODAY. FORCING FOR ASCENT ASSOCIATED WITH THIS FEATURE WILL LIKELY PROMOTE WIDELY SCATTERED TSTM DEVELOPMENT ALONG THE DRYLINE THIS AFTERNOON FROM PORTIONS OF S-CNTRL NEB/N-CNTRL KS INTO WRN TX. THE 12Z ABQ SOUNDING SAMPLED 40 KT SWLY FLOW IN THE 4-5 KM AGL LAYER WHICH SHOULD ENHANCE VERTICAL SHEAR AMIDST A THERMODYNAMIC ENVIRONMENT CHARACTERIZED BY MLCAPE OF 2000-3000+ J/KG. AS SUCH...THE POTENTIAL WILL EXIST FOR SUPERCELL AND ORGANIZED MULTICELL MORPHOLOGIES WITH A RISK FOR DAMAGING WINDS AND LARGE HAIL. A SEPARATE AREA OF TSTMS MAY EVOLVE THIS AFTERNOON WITHIN AN INCREASING LOW-LEVEL UPSLOPE REGIME DEVELOPING WITHIN THE POST-FRONTAL ENVIRONMENT FROM THE CHEYENNE RIDGE TO PALMER DIVIDE. AMPLE VERTICAL SHEAR AND SUFFICIENT BUOYANCY WILL EXIST FOR ORGANIZED STORMS INCLUDING SUPERCELLS WITH A LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND THREAT DEVELOPING FROM SERN WY/NERN CO INTO PARTS OF WRN NEB BY LATE THIS EVENING. ...GREAT LAKES/MIDWEST INTO MID ATLANTIC THIS AFTERNOON INTO TONIGHT... sections.title: GREAT LAKES/MIDWEST INTO MID ATLANTIC
sections.text: UNCERTAINTY REMAINS REGARDING CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT/EVOLUTION ACROSS PARTS OF PA INTO THE MID ATLANTIC IN THE WAKE OF EARLIER CONVECTION. THE EWD PROPAGATING MCS OVER LOWER MI/IND WILL LIKELY CONTINUE EWD ACROSS NRN OH AND MAY PERSIST INTO PA. OTHER MODEL GUIDANCE CONTINUES TO INDICATE STRONG STORMS DEVELOPING DURING THE EVENING/OVERNIGHT AHEAD OF THE SWD SAGGING COLD FRONT ACROSS CNTRL PA. ALTHOUGH CONFIDENCE IS LOW...A MOIST/UNSTABLE AIRMASS WITH SUFFICIENT DEEP LAYER SHEAR IN THE VICINITY OF A COLD FRONT AND OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES WOULD SUPPORT SEVERE STORMS IF THEY DEVELOP/ORGANIZE. THEREFORE WILL REFRAIN FROM REMOVING/LOWERING PROBABILITIES ACROSS EASTERN PORTIONS OF THE SLIGHT RISK AT THIS TIME. ELSEWHERE...PREVIOUS FORECAST REMAINS UNCHANGED WITH SCATTERED STRONG/SEVERE STORMS UNDERWAY ACROSS PORTIONS OF THE PLAINS. REF MCD 1062 AND 1063 FOR MORE DETAILS. ..LEITMAN.. 06/18/2014 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1124 AM CDT WED JUN 18 2014/

OTHERWISE...IT STILL APPEARS POSSIBLE THAT STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS NOW MOVING THROUGH THE UPPER OHIO VALLEY COULD CROSS THE CENTRAL APPALACHIANS AND PROVIDE A RISK FOR POTENTIALLY DAMAGING WIND GUSTS ACROSS PARTS OF THE NORTHERN MID ATLANTIC COAST STATES LATER TONIGHT.

sections.title: PLAINS AND MID MO/UPPER MS VALLEY REGION
sections.text: VERY WARM AND STRONGLY CAPPING ELEVATED MIXED LAYER AIR...EXTENDING IN A PLUME FROM THE SOUTHERN U.S./MEXICAN PLATEAU REGION NORTHEASTWARD INTO THE UPPER MISSISSIPPI VALLEY...IS CONTRIBUTING TO SOME UNCERTAINTY CONCERNING CONTINUING SEVERE WEATHER POTENTIAL INTO THE OVERNIGHT HOURS. SCATTERED STORMS CURRENTLY ONGOING THROUGHOUT THE PLAINS SEEM LIKELY TO BEGIN TO WEAKEN AND DIMINISH IN COVERAGE WITH THE ONSET OF BOUNDARY LAYER COOLING. THE PRIMARY EXCEPTION APPEARS TO EXIST NEAR A WARM FRONTAL ZONE ACROSS SOUTHEASTERN SOUTH DAKOTA...ALONG WHICH BOUNDARY LAYER INSTABILITY REMAINS STRONG TO EXTREME /MIXED-LAYER CAPE ON THE ORDER OF 4000+ J PER KG/ BENEATH STEEP MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES. DEEP-LAYER SHEAR IS WEAK ACROSS THIS REGION...BUT LOW-LEVEL HODOGRAPHS ARE SIZABLE BENEATH 30+ KT SOUTHERLY 850 MB FLOW. FOCUSED LOW-LEVEL CONVERGENCE EAST OF A WEAK SURFACE LOW /NOW WEST SOUTHWEST OF SIOUX FALLS/ MAY STILL CONTRIBUTE TO CONSIDERABLE UPSCALE CONVECTIVE GROWTH THIS EVENING...AS A SHORT WAVE IMPULSE MIGRATES NORTH NORTHEAST OF THE CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS...AROUND THE PERIPHERY OF THE MORE PROMINENT SLOW MOVING MID/UPPER LOW ACROSS MONTANA. IF/WHEN THIS OCCURS...ACTIVITY PROBABLY WILL TEND TO PR

sections.title: UPPER OHIO VALLEY INTO MID ATLANTIC COAST
sections.text: A LINE OF STORMS PERSISTS ACROSS THE UPPER OHIO VALLEY...AHEAD OF A SHORT WAVE TROUGH PROGRESSING EAST SOUTHEAST OF THE GREAT LAKES REGION. 30+ KT 500 MB FLOW ON THE SOUTHERN FRINGE OF THE STRONGER WESTERLIES IS CONTRIBUTING TO A MODESTLY FAST SYSTEM MOTION...WHICH SHOULD PROGRESS CONVECTION EAST OF THE CENTRAL APPALACHIANS AROUND OR SHORTLY AFTER 06Z. AS THIS OCCURS...A RESIDUAL MOIST AND POTENTIALLY MODERATELY UNSTABLE AIR MASS ACROSS THE MID ATLANTIC REGION /WHERE STRONG AFTERNOON HEATING OCCURRED/COULD SUPPORT REINTENSIFICATION OF CONVECTION AND CONTRIBUTE TO THE RISK FOR POTENTIALLY DAMAGING WIND GUSTS. ..KERR.. 06/19/2014

mesoscale_discussions.summary: STORMS ADVANCING ACROSS SRN LAKE MI ATTM WILL MOVE INTO/ACROSS THE SRN LOWER MI VICINITY OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS. A SOMEWHAT CONVECTIVELY STABILIZED AIRMASS DOWNSTREAM SUGGESTS THAT SEVERE THREAT MAY BE LIMITED/LOCALIZED -- AT LEAST INITIALLY...BUT WW COULD BECOME NECESSARY WITH TIME.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LATEST RADAR LOOP SHOWS A WELL-DEFINED BOW ECHO MOVING ACROSS SRN PORTIONS OF LAKE MI ATTM...AND WILL BEGIN TO SHIFT INTO SRN LOWER MI IN THE NEXT HOUR OR SO. THE AIRMASS DOWNSTREAM OF THIS MCS HAS BEEN SOMEWHAT STABILIZED BY EARLIER CONVECTION...WITH BETTER INSTABILITY CONFINED TO AREAS NEAR AND S OF THE SRN BORDER OF LOWER MI. STILL...THE DEGREE OF ORGANIZATION OF THIS BOW AS INDICATED BY RADAR SUGGESTS THAT LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS ALONG WITH MARGINAL HAIL MAY STILL BE POSSIBLE AS THE BOW MOVES EWD ACROSS THE REGION AT 40 KT. IN ADDITION...SOME RISK THAT INTENSIFICATION ALONG THE SRN FLANK OF THE BOW SEEMS TO EXIST GIVEN THE MORE FAVORABLE THERMODYNAMIC ENVIRONMENT INTO INDIANA/OH -- DESPITE INDICATIONS TO THE CONTRARY WITHIN RECENT WRF-HRRR RUNS. WE WILL CONTINUE TO MONITOR THE EVOLUTION OF THIS MCS -- PARTICULARLY ON ITS SRN FRINGE -- FOR SIGNS THAT A WW MAY BECOME NECESSARY.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: STORMS/SEVERE RISK EXPECTED TO GRADUALLY INCREASE ACROSS THE DISCUSSION AREA...WITH A TORNADO WATCH LIKELY REQUIRED WITHIN THE NEXT HOUR OR SO.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LATEST SURFACE AND OBJECTIVE ANALYSES INDICATE A HEATING/DESTABILIZING AIRMASS ACROSS THE DAKOTAS ATTM...NEAR AND E OF AN INVERTED TROUGH EXTENDING NNWWD FROM A LOW ANALYZED NEAR THE SD/NEB BORDER JUST NE OF ANW. ELY/SELY LOW-LEVEL FLOW E OF THE TROUGH/N OF THE LOW BENEATH MODERATE SWLYS AT MID LEVELS IS YIELDING SHEAR SUPPORTIVE OF ORGANIZED/ROTATING STORMS...WHICH COMBINED WITH ONGOING AIRMASS DESTABILIZATION WILL SUPPORT A CONTINUED RAMP-UP IN SEVERE RISK THIS AFTERNOON. ALONG WITH POTENTIAL FOR VERY LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS...DEGREE OF LOW-LEVEL SHEAR AND LOW LCLS ALSO SUGGESTS POTENTIAL FOR A FEW TORNADOES. AS SUCH...TORNADO WATCH ISSUANCE IS EXPECTED WITHIN THE HOUR.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: CONVECTIVE INITIATION IS EXPECTED WITHIN THE NEXT HOUR OR TWO ACROSS THE SRN HIGH PLAINS. SCATTERED STRONG TO SVR TSTMS ARE EXPECTED WITH ONE OR MORE WATCHES POSSIBLY NEEDED TO COVER THE THREAT. PRIMARY SVR THREAT WILL LIKELY BE SVR HAIL WITH A SECONDARY THREAT OF DAMAGING WINDS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY SHOWS INCREASED CU ACROSS SW KS AND ALONG THE TX/NM BORDER E OF CVS. MID/UPPER LEVEL CLOUDINESS MAY BE OBSCURING SOME CU AROUND AMA AS WELL. DIURNAL HEATING CONTINUES TO DESTABILIZE AN ENVIRONMENT CHARACTERIZED BY DEWPOINTS IN THE LOW TO MID 60S AND STEEP MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES. SURFACE ANALYSIS REVEALS A DUAL DRYLINE STRUCTURE WITH THE LEADING DRYLINE EXTENDING FROM SW KS SSWWD ACROSS THE OK AND TX PANHANDLES AND TX S PLAINS. THE SECONDARY DRYLINE EXTENDS SWD FROM A LOW IN SE CO ACROSS FAR WRN NM. TSTM DEVELOPMENT IS MOST LIKELY ALONG THE LEADING DRYLINE BUT SOME ADDITIONAL DEVELOPMENT IS POSSIBLE ALONG THE SECONDARY DRYLINE. SATELLITE IMAGERY ALSO REVEALS A SHORTWAVE TROUGH OVER NE NM MOVING INTO SW KS. OBJECTIVE ANALYSIS ESTIMATES MLCAPE FROM 1500 TO 2500 J PER KG ALONG AND AHEAD OF THE LEADING DRYLINE. LOW-LEVEL SWLY FLOW IS GENERALLY AROUND 10 TO 15 KT WITH REGIONAL VAD WIND PROFILES SUGGESTING MID-LEVEL SWLY FLOW AROUND 20 KT. THE RESULT IS A WEAKLY SHEARED PROFILE. HOWEVER...BULK SHEAR WILL GRADUALLY INCREASE THROUGHOUT THE AFTERNOON AND INTO THE EVENING WITH STORMS EXPECTED TO GRADUALLY INTENSIFY AS THEY MOVE EWD. SCATTERED STRONG TO SEVERE TSTMS ARE EXPECTED WITH THE PRIMARY THREAT OF SEVERE HAIL. SOME DAMAGING WINDS ARE ALSO POSSIBLE. ONE OR MORE WATCHES MAY BE NEEDED TO ADDRESS THIS SVR THREAT.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: STORMS INCREASING ACROSS PARTS OF CENTRAL IL AND CENTRAL INDIANA AS THE AIRMASS REACHES PEAK AFTERNOON DESTABILIZATION. SEVERE RISK REMAINS ISOLATED...BUT COULD REQUIRE WW IF STORMS ORGANIZE UPSCALE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LATEST SURFACE AND OBJECTIVE ANALYSES REVEAL A VERY WARM/MOIST/UNSTABLE AIRMASS ACROSS THE DISCUSSION AREA...WITH TEMPERATURES NEAR 90 AND DEWPOINTS IN THE LOW 70S SUPPORTING MIXED-LAYER CAPE AROUND 3000 J/KG. WHILE STRONGER/MORE ORGANIZED CONVECTION REMAINS OVER LOWER MI AND NRN INDIANA...STORMS TRAILING WWD INTO E CENTRAL IL NEAR AND AHEAD OF THE REMNANT OUTFLOW BOUNDARY CONTINUE TO INCREASE...WITH A SMALL CLUSTER OF CONVECTION NOW OVER THE IROQUOIS/FORD/CHAMPAIGN/VERMILION COUNTY VICINITY OF IL SHOWING SOME BOWING TENDENCY. WHILE FLOW IN THE LOWEST 4-5 KM REMAINS RELATIVELY MODEST /AOB 20 KT PER AREA VWPS/...THE DEGREE OF DEEP-LAYER SHEAR MAY BE SUFFICIENT -- GIVEN THE FAVORABLE THERMODYNAMIC ENVIRONMENT -- TO SUPPORT SOME INCREASE IN STORM ORGANIZATION/LONGEVITY. SOME HIGH-RES CONVECTION-ALLOWING RUNS CONTINUE TO HINT AT POTENTIAL FOR A MORE ORGANIZED/BOWING CLUSTER MOVING SEWD ACROSS THIS AREA THROUGH SUNSET...AND THIS EVOLUTION WOULD LIKELY BE ACCOMPANIED BY A MORE SUBSTANTIAL SEVERE RISK WHICH COULD REQUIRE WW ISSUANCE.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SEVERE/TORNADO RISK IS GRADUALLY INCREASING ATTM ACROSS THE DISCUSSION AREA...WITH TORNADO WATCH ISSUANCE POSSIBLE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LATEST VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY SHOWS A GRADUALLY INCREASING/DEEPENING CU FIELD ACROSS SERN SD AND ADJACENT NRN NEB...NEAR AND E OF A SURFACE LOW ANALYZED E OF ANW ATTM. A MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER INVOF THE LOW AND THE ASSOCIATED/ESEWD-ALIGNED WARM FRONT HAS BECOME STRONGLY UNSTABLE WITH AFTERNOON HEATING...WITH MIXED-LAYER CAPE IN EXCESS OF 4000 J/KG INDICATED. THE DEGREE OF INSTABILITY COMBINED WITH LOW-LEVEL SELY FLOW VEERING TO SWLY WITH HEIGHT AND INCREASING TO 30-40 KT AT MID LEVELS IS YIELDING AN ENVIRONMENT QUITE SUPPORTIVE OF SUPERCELLS -- AND ASSOCIATED SEVERE/TORNADO POTENTIAL. WE WILL CONTINUE TO MONITOR EVOLUTION OF THE CU FIELD ACROSS THIS REGION FOR TIMING OF POSSIBLE WW ISSUANCE.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ONGOING LINE OF TSTMS IS EXPECTED TO CONTINUE EWD/SEWD INTO CNTRL AND WRN OH WITH A SOME RESULTANT SVR THREAT POSSIBLE DOWNSTREAM OF WW 321.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: RECENT RADAR IMAGERY CONTINUES TO REVEAL A WELL-DEVELOPED LINE OF TSTMS EXTENDING FROM E-CNTRL LWR MI SWWD INTO NE IND...MOVING EWD/SEWD AT 40 KT. TRENDS INDICATE THE STRONGEST PORTION OF THIS LINE...ROUGHLY FROM DFI NEWD TO JUST W OF VLL...WILL LIKELY CONTINUE EWD INTO ONTARIO. SRN PORTION OF THE LINE IS EXPECTED TO EXHIBIT A MORE SELY MOTION INTO THE INSTABILITY ACROSS E-CNTRL IND AND WRN OH. ONGOING ACTIVITY ACROSS THIS REGION SUGGESTS THE SYSTEM SHOULD MAINTAIN ITS CURRENT STRENGTH WITH SOME FORWARD-PROPAGATION POSSIBLE. HOWEVER...MOST RECENT REGIONAL RADAR IMAGERY IS BEGINNING TO SHOW THE OUTFLOW SURGING AHEAD OF THE SRN PORTION OF THE LINE...INTRODUCING UNCERTAINTY INTO THE SYSTEM/S ABILITY OF MAINTAINING A DAMAGING WIND TREAT. TRENDS ACROSS THE AREA WILL BE MONITORED FOR POTENTIAL WW.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: BAND OF THUNDERSTORMS AND ASSOCIATED SEVERE RISK MOVING STEADILY EWD ACROSS WW 321.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LATEST RADAR LOOP SHOWS A BROKEN LINE OF STORMS -- WITH EMBEDDED BOWING STRUCTURES -- MOVING EWD AT ROUGHLY 40 KT ACROSS SERN LOWER MI AND ADJACENT NERN INDIANA/NWRN OH. STORMS OVER SERN MI WILL MOVE INTO SRN ONTARIO AND ADJACENT LK ERIE SHORTLY...ENDING THE MAIN SEVERE RISK ACROSS LOWER MI. MEANWHILE...THE PORTION OF THE LINE OF STORMS CROSSING NERN INDIANA AND NWRN OH SHOULD CONTINUE ADVANCING EWD INTO MORE OF WRN AND NRN OH...WHERE AT LEAST ISOLATED SEVERE RISK IS EVIDENT. WE WILL CONTINUE TO MONITOR AREAS DOWNSTREAM OF WW 321 FOR NEW WW ISSUANCE...AND IN THE MEAN TIME SEVERE THREAT CONTINUES ACROSS VALID PORTIONS OF WW 321.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A POTENTIAL FOR A COUPLE TORNADOES...ISOLATED LARGE HAIL AND WIND DAMAGE SHOULD CONTINUE ACROSS SCNTRL ND AND NCNTRL SD INTO EARLY THIS EVENING. THE THREAT IS EXPECTED TO SPREAD NEWD INTO SERN ND AND NERN SD WHERE A LOCAL WW EXTENSION OR NEW WW MAY BECOME NECESSARY.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SFC ANALYSIS AT 22Z SHOWS A 1001 MB LOW TO THE WEST OF YANKTON SD WITH AN INVERTED TROUGH EXTENDING NNWWD ACROSS NCNTRL SD. MESOANALYSIS SUGGESTS THAT MODERATE INSTABILITY IS LOCATED ALONG THE TROUGH WHERE MLCAPE IS ESTIMATED IN THE 2000 TO 2500 J/KG RANGE. IN ADDITION...THE ABERDEEN WSR-88 VWP SHOWS 0-6 KM SHEAR OF 35 TO 40 KT WITH 0-3 KM STORM RELATIVE HELICITY OF 230 M2/S2. THIS ENVIRONMENT WILL CONTINUE TO SUPPORT AN ISOLATED TORNADO THREAT AS CELLS MOVE ACROSS THE NERN PART OF WW 322 OVER THE NEXT 1 TO 2 HOURS. USING EXISTING STORM MOTIONS...THE STORMS SHOULD AFFECT AREAS TO THE NORTHEAST OF WW 322 AFTER 01Z WHERE A LOCAL EXTENSION IN AREA OR NEW WW MAY BE BECOME NECESSARY. FURTHER TO THE WEST ACROSS PARTS OF SWRN ND AND WCNTRL SD...SFC WINDS ARE NWLY AND THE AIRMASS HAS BECOME LESS FAVORABLE FOR SEVERE STORMS. FOR THIS REASON...STARK...HETTINGER AND ADAMS COUNTIES IN ND AND PERKINS...ZIEBACH AND HAAKON COUNTIES IN SD MAY BE REMOVED AT 23Z.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THREAT FOR PRIMARILY STRONG TO MARGINALLY SVR WINDS WILL CONTINUE TO EXPAND S/EWD INTO THE LATE EVENING. THE POTENTIAL FOR NEW WW ISSUANCE FROM SERN IND ENEWD INTO WRN PA WILL BE CONTINGENT ON TRENDS FOR INCREASING COLD-POOL STRENGTH AND ASSOCIATED MAGNITUDE OF THE WIND THREAT.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A COLD POOL EMANATING OUT OF THE SRN END OF A QUASI-LINEAR CONVECTIVE SYSTEM OVER CNTRL IND AND NWRN OH IS MERGING WITH MORE DISCRETE TSTM DEVELOPMENT OCCURRING TO THE S...ACROSS S-CNTRL IND AND W-CNTRL OH...AND MORE RECENTLY ACROSS NWRN PA. LATEST STORM REPORTS ARE CONSISTENT WITH OBSERVATIONAL AND RADAR TRENDS INDICATING STRONG TO MARGINALLY SVR WIND GUSTS...AS WELL AS SMALL HAIL...ARE POSSIBLE WITH THE STRONGER UPDRAFT PULSES. TRENDS CONTINUE TO INDICATE BOTH THE COLD POOL AND ACCOMPANYING CONVECTION ARE NOT PARTICULARLY WELL-ORGANIZED...BUT DOWNSTREAM ENVIRONMENT REMAINS MOIST AND UNSTABLE /MLCAPE 1500-2500 J/KG PER RAP OBJECTIVE ANALYSIS/. WITH 20-30 KT OF AMBIENT WLY DEEP-LAYER FLOW...THREAT FOR STRONG TO MARGINALLY SVR WIND GUSTS SHOULD PERSIST...WITH WW ISSUANCE PREDICATED ON INCREASING ORGANIZATIONAL TRENDS WITH ONGOING CONVECTION.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: AN ISOLATED THREAT FOR LARGE HAIL MAY ACCOMPANY RECENT TSTM DEVELOPMENT ACROSS NRN IL...BUT DOES NOT APPEAR SUFFICIENT FOR WW ISSUANCE ATTM.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: RADAR MOSAIC SHOWS INCREASING CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT OCCURRING WITHIN A GENERAL W-E CORRIDOR...POSITIONED FROM JUST E OF DBQ EWD TO NEAR CHICAGO. THIS APPEARS TO BE OCCURRING TO THE IMMEDIATE N OF A WEAK COLD FRONT EXTENDING WWD FROM A SFC LOW OVER LOWER MI...WITH A SEPARATE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY LOCATED FARTHER S TO NEAR MLI. THE AIR MASS TO THE N OF THESE BOUNDARIES HAS GRADUALLY MODIFIED IN THE WAKE OF EARLIER CONVECTION...WITH PROXIMITY SFC OBS SHOWING UPPER 70S TO LOWER 80S F TEMPERATURES. TSTMS APPEAR LIKELY TO PERSIST FOR AT LEAST THE NEXT 1-2 HRS ACROSS NRN IL AS AN INFLUX OF HIGHER THETA-E AIR TO THE SW IS MAINTAINED...AMIDST STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES. MUCAPE VALUES ARE ESTIMATED AT 1500-2000 J/KG PER RAP OBJECTIVE ANALYSIS. AS A RESULT...PRIMARY THREAT APPEARS TO BE ISOLATED INSTANCES OF LARGE HAIL...AND PERHAPS STRONG-MARGINALLY SVR WIND GUSTS WITH STRONGER UPDRAFT PULSES.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A POTENTIAL FOR HAIL AND ISOLATED DAMAGING WIND GUSTS WILL LIKELY CONTINUE WITH THE STRONGER CELLS ACROSS PARTS OF WW 324 AND WW 323 OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS. DUE TO THE ISOLATED NATURE OF THE THREAT AND DUE TO DECREASING INSTABILITY...WW ISSUANCE BEYOND THE 03Z EXPIRATION IS NOT ANTICIPATED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: THE LATEST SFC ANALYSIS SHOWS A 1000-MB LOW OVER SERN CO WITH A TROUGH EXTENDING SSWWD ACROSS FAR ERN NM. SLY TO SELY FLOW IS LOCATED TO THE EAST OF THE SFC TROUGH ACROSS MUCH OF THE SRN AND CNTRL PLAINS WHERE SFC DEWPOINTS GENERALLY RANGE FROM THE MID 50S TO MID 60S F. MLCAPE IS ESTIMATED TO BE IN THE 1500 TO 2500 J/KG RANGE ACROSS WRN KS AND THE TX PANHANDLE. IN SPITE OF MODERATE INSTABILITY...THE SEVERE THREAT REMAINS MORE ISOLATED DUE TO RELATIVELY WEAK DEEP-LAYER SHEAR PROFILES EVIDENT ON THE DODGE CITY AND AMARILLO WSR-88D VWPS WITH 0-6 KM SHEAR MAGNITUDE OF LESS THAN 30 KT. THE MODERATE INSTABILITY COMBINED WITH STEEP MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES SHOULD SUPPORT AN ISOLATED LARGE-HAIL THREAT MAINLY ACROSS THE ERN PART OF WW 323 AND WW 324 WHERE INSTABILITY IS GREATEST. ISOLATED DAMAGING WIND GUSTS MAY ALSO OCCUR WITH THE MORE INTENSE DOWNDRAFTS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: MARGINALLY SEVERE WIND GUSTS AND HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE ACROSS NE CO AND SW NEB EARLY THIS EVENING. THE THREAT IS EXPECTED TO REMAIN TOO ISOLATED TO WARRANT WW ISSUANCE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: THE LATEST SFC ANALYSIS SHOWS A 1000-MB LOW OVER SE CO WITH UPSLOPE FLOW IN PLACE ACROSS MOST OF NERN CO. THUNDERSTORMS ARE DEVELOPING ALONG THE FRONT RANGE WHERE SFC DEWPOINTS ARE IN THE UPPER 30S F AND INSTABILITY IS WEAK. THE ACTIVITY IS LOCATED IN THE RIGHT REAR QUADRANT OF A JET NEAR 500 MB. THE JET IS ENHANCING DEEP-LAYER SHEAR ACROSS NERN CO WHERE THE MAGNITUDE OF 0-6 KM SHEAR IS ESTIMATED IN THE 50 TO 60 KT RANGE. THIS COMBINED WITH STEEP LAPSE RATES MAY BE ENOUGH FOR STRONG WIND GUSTS AND HAIL AS CELLS MOVE NEWD INTO THE CO HIGH PLAINS EARLY THIS EVENING. FURTHER TO THE EAST ACROSS SWRN NEB...ISOLATED CELLS HAVE INITIATED NEAR OGALLALA NEB IN AN AREA OF ENHANCED LOW-LEVEL CONVERGENCE. THE 00Z SOUNDING AT NORTH PLATTE NEB SHOWS MUCAPE NEAR 3000 J/KG WITH 0-6 KM SHEAR NEAR 35 KT. THIS COMBINED WITH 0-3 KM LAPSE RATE OF 9.0 C/KM SHOULD BE SUFFICIENT FOR ISOLATED DAMAGING WIND GUSTS. THE MODERATE INSTABILITY MAY ALSO SUPPORT A HAIL THREAT.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SEMI-ORGANIZED CONVECTIVE LINE CONTINUES TO PROGRESS EWD ACROSS OH AND WRN PA...WITH ISOLATED DISCRETE TSTM DEVELOPMENT OCCURRING AHEAD OF THE LINE. PRIMARY THREAT APPEARS TO BE DMGG WIND GUSTS...WHILE HAIL MAY ALSO ACCOMPANY THE MORE DISCRETE ACTIVITY. A NEW DOWNSTREAM WW MAY BE NEEDED WITHIN THE NEXT HR TO INCLUDE PARTS OF NRN WV...CNTRL PA...THE MD PANHANDLE...AND EXTREME NRN VA.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: RECENT RADAR MOSAIC IMAGERY SHOWS SEMI-CONTINUOUS CONVECTIVE LINE AND ACCOMPANYING COLD POOL EXTENDING FROM NEAR LUK NEWD TO FKL AS OF 0045Z. OBSERVATIONS SUGGEST STRONG-MARGINALLY SVR WIND GUSTS ARE ACCOMPANYING THIS LINE...CONSISTENT WITH NUMEROUS REPORTS OF DOWNED TREES. DISCRETE TSTMS ARE ALSO DEVELOPING AHEAD OF THE LINE ACROSS WRN/CNTRL PA...AND ARE EXHIBITING OCCASIONAL POTENTIAL FOR LARGE HAIL IN ADDITION TO STRONG WIND GUSTS. 00Z SOUNDING FROM PBZ SAMPLED A VERY MOIST/UNSTABLE AIR MASS...WITH MLCAPE VALUES EXCEEDING 2000 J/KG AND 20-30 KT OF NEARLY UNIFORM WLY DEEP-LAYER FLOW. ENVIRONMENT REMAINS FAVORABLE FOR SUSTENANCE OF CONVECTION DESPITE THE IMMINENT ONSET OF DIURNAL COOLING...ESPECIALLY S OF A QUASI-STATIONARY BOUNDARY BISECTING PA WHICH DELINEATES A SLIGHTLY WARMER/MORE MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER TO THE S. EXTENT/MAGNITUDE OF THE DOWNSTREAM DMGG WIND THREAT WILL CONTINUE TO BE PREDICATED ON THE DEGREE OF ORGANIZATION CONVECTION CAN MAINTAIN...AND MAY REQUIRE A NEW WW DOWNSTREAM FROM WW 326 WITHIN THE NEXT HR...TO INCLUDE PARTS OF CNTRL PA...WV...THE MD PANHANDLE...AND EXTREME NRN VA.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A TORNADO THREAT ALONG WITH POTENTIAL FOR LARGE HAIL AND WIND DAMAGE...ARE EXPECTED TO CONTINUE ACROSS SE ND AND ERN SD THROUGH LATE THIS EVENING. THE THREAT MAY PERSIST INTO THE OVERNIGHT PERIOD.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: THE LATEST SFC ANALYSIS SHOWS A 1002-MB LOW OVER ERN SD WITH A WELL-DEFINED INVERTED TROUGH EXTENDING NNWWD INTO SERN ND. A NEARLY CONTINUOUS LINE OF STORMS IS ONGOING ALONG THE TROUGH. THE STORMS ARE LOCATED IN A VERY MOIST ENVIRONMENT WITH SFC DEWPOINTS NEAR 70 F AND MLCAPE ESTIMATED FROM NEAR 2000 J/KG IN SE ND TO AROUND 4000 J/KG IN ERN SD. IN ADDITION TO THE STRONG INSTABILITY...REGIONAL WSR-88D VWPS SHOW VEERING WINDS WITH HEIGHT BELOW 3 KM WITH 0-3 KM STORM RELATIVE HELICITY AROUND 250 M2/S2. THIS STRONG LOW-LEVEL SHEAR SHOULD CONTINUE TO BE FAVORABLE FOR TORNADIC STORMS LATE THIS EVENING. IN ADDITION TO A FEW TORNADOES...LARGE HAIL AND WIND DAMAGE WILL ALSO BE POSSIBLE WITH SUPERCELLS OR SMALL BOWS EMBEDDED IN THE LINE.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: AN ISOLATED SEVERE THREAT IS EXPECTED TO CONTINUE THROUGH LATE THIS EVENING ACROSS SCNTRL AND SERN NEB. LARGE HAIL AND WIND DAMAGE SHOULD BE THE PRIMARY THREATS. WW ISSUANCE REMAINS POSSIBLE ACROSS THE MCD AREA.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: THE LATEST SFC ANALYSIS SHOWS A 1002-MB LOW OVER SERN SD WITH A QUASI-STATIONARY FRONT EXTENDING SWWD ACROSS CNTRL NEB INTO NW KS. A SEVERE THUNDERSTORM IS ONGOING IN PHILLIPS COUNTY KS WHERE LOW-LEVEL CONVERGENCE APPEARS TO BE ENHANCED. THE ACTIVITY APPEARS TO BE SUPPORTED BY A SHORTWAVE TROUGH EVIDENT ON WATER VAPOR IMAGERY OVER WCNTRL KS. SFC DEWPOINTS IN THE PATH OF THE STORM ARE NEAR 70 F AND MLCAPE IS ESTIMATED IN THE 3000 TO 4000 J/KG RANGE. THE STRONG INSTABILITY SHOULD ENABLE THE STORM TO HAVE A SEVERE THREAT LATE THIS EVENING. STEEP LOW TO MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES SHOULD MAKE WIND DAMAGE AND HAIL A POSSIBILITY. THE SEVERE THREAT MAY DECREASE TOWARD MIDNIGHT AS INSTABILITY BEGINS TO DECREASE ACROSS THE REGION.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: CLUSTER OF TSTMS PROGRESSING SEWD ACROSS NWRN IND IS EXHIBITING POTENTIAL FOR STRONG WIND GUSTS. IT IS UNCERTAIN HOW FAR SWD THIS THREAT WILL EXTEND INTO THE LATE EVENING...BUT TRENDS ARE BEING MONITORED FOR A POSSIBLE WW.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: CONVECTION THAT DEVELOPED OVER NRN IL HAS PERSISTED WITH SEWD PROGRESSION INTO NWRN IND...CURRENTLY POSITIONED WITHIN A MODIFIED AIR MASS N OF AN OUTFLOW BOUNDARY DRAPED NW-SE ACROSS THE AREA. THE 00Z ILX SOUNDING MODIFIED WITH PROXIMITY SFC OBS SUGGEST THIS CONVECTION MAY BE SLIGHTLY ELEVATED. HOWEVER...RECENT RADAR IMAGES FROM LOT/IND SAMPLED VERY STRONG VELOCITIES AT AROUND 5000-6000 FT AGL...WHICH MAY BE SUFFICIENT FOR PRODUCING STRONG-SVR WIND GUSTS. CURRENT MOTION EXTRAPOLATION SUGGESTS ONGOING CONVECTION SHOULD REMAIN TO THE N OF THE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY WITHIN A RELATIVELY LESS UNSTABLE AIR MASS. WHILE STILL UNCERTAIN...THERE IS SOME CONCERN THAT CONVECTION COULD MAINTAIN OR INCREASE IN INTENSITY WITH SWD PROGRESSION INTO A SLIGHTLY MORE UNSTABLE AIR MASS IN PROXIMITY TO THE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY. ADDITIONALLY...RECENT OBSERVATIONAL TRENDS SHOW A GRADUAL INCREASE IN SFC DEWPOINTS IS OCCURRING N OF THE BOUNDARY ACROSS CNTRL IND. CONVECTIVE TRENDS WILL CONTINUE TO BE MONITORED FOR A POSSIBLE WW SHOULD A MORE WIDESPREAD THREAT FOR SVR WIND GUSTS BECOME APPARENT.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SVR POTENTIAL MAY INCREASE ACROSS THIS AREA OVER NEXT 3-4 HOURS WITH TWO INITIALLY SEPARATE BUT POTENTIALLY MERGING AREAS OF TSTMS IN SWRN MN AND ERN DAKOTAS. SOME PART OF THIS AREA MAY REQUIRE WW.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SFC MESOANALYSIS SHOWED LOW OVER E-CENTRAL SD NEAR TAIL END OF QLCS...AND ALONG OUTFLOW BOUNDARY THAT ARCS GENERALLY SWD OVER NERN NEB. WARM FRONT WAS EVIDENT FROM LOW ESEWD OVER SWRN CORNER OF MN AND N-CENTRAL IA...AND SHOULD SHIFT NWD 10-15 KT THROUGH REMAINDER EVENING. CLUSTERS OF SCATTERED TSTMS HAVE DEVELOPED OVER SWRN MN AS LOW-LEVEL WAA AND MOISTURE TRANSPORT STRENGTHENS IN ASSOCIATION WITH LLJ. ALTHOUGH CONVECTION IS AND SHOULD REMAIN N OF WARM FRONT...MODIFICATIONS TO OAX/MPX/ABR RAOBS SUGGEST SURFACE-BASED EFFECTIVE INFLOW PARCELS CURRENTLY ARE POSSIBLE ROUGHLY S OF MKT-VVV LINE. OFFSETTING STABILIZING EFFECTS WILL BECOME MORE IMPORTANT--NAMELY GROWING TSTM/OUTFLOW COVERAGE AND GRADUAL DIABATIC SFC COOLING AMIDST MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER. VERTICAL SHEAR N OF WARM FRONT IS FAVORABLE FOR SUPERCELLS...WITH EFFECTIVE SRH 400-500 J/KG. AS SUCH...LARGE HAIL AND SVR GUSTS ARE POSSIBLE...AND A TORNADO OR TWO CANNOT BE RULED OUT. HOWEVER...MODAL PROBLEMS...MAINLY WITH TSTM CLUSTERING...ALSO COULD MITIGATE HAIL/TORNADO RISK TO SOME EXTENT. MEANWHILE...QLCS INITIALLY MOVING SLOWLY EWD/NEWD OVER WWS 327/328 MAY POSE RISK OF DAMAGING WIND AS IT MOVES INTO STABILIZING BUT STILL AT LEAST MARGINALLY FAVORABLE AIR MASS ACROSS ERN ND AND W-CENTRAL/NWRN MN. MLCINH STRENGTHENS CONSIDERABLY WITH NWD EXTENT FROM MSP-FAR STRETCH OF I-94 AND NEWD FROM FOSTER COUNTY ND...INDICATING CORRESPONDING LESSENING OF ORGANIZED WIND POTENTIAL. WITHIN TRIANGULAR WEDGE OF AIR BETWEEN CINH LINE...QLCS AND WARM FRONT...MLCAPE INCREASED FROM AROUND 1500 J/KG OVER SERN ND TO 4500 J/KG ALONG WARM FRONT...AMIDST 30-40 KT EFFECTIVE-SHEAR MAGNITUDES. ..EDWARDS.. 06/19/2014 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A SEVERE THREAT IS EXPECTED TO CONTINUE FROM SW NEB EXTENDING NEWD INTO CNTRL NEB OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS. WW ISSUANCE WILL LIKELY BE NEEDED ACROSS THE REGION SOON.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: CONVECTIVE CLUSTER...CURRENTLY JUST SOUTH OF JULESBURG CO IS EXPECTED TO CONTINUE FOR SEVERAL MORE HOURS AS IT ENCOUNTERS GREATER INSTABILITY TO THE EAST ACROSS WRN AND CNTRL NEB. THE 01Z HRRR MODEL SUGGESTS THAT THIS CLUSTER WILL CONTINUE TO EXPAND IN COVERAGE ACROSS THE NORTH PLATTE VCNTY...EVENTUALLY REACHING THE NORFOLK AREA LATER TONIGHT. MODERATE TO STRONG INSTABILITY...40 TO 50 KT OF DEEP-LAYER SHEAR AND STEEP LAPSE RATES WILL CONTINUE TO SUPPORT A SEVERE THREAT. LARGE HAIL AND WIND DAMAGE ARE EXPECTED TO BE THE PRIMARY THREATS. THE WIND-DAMAGE THREAT MAY BECOME LOCALLY ENHANCED WITH CELL MERGERS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE WIND DAMAGE THREAT MAY CONTINUE THROUGH PART OF THE OVERNIGHT PERIOD ACROSS SRN PA...NRN MD AND ERN WV. DUE TO THE ISOLATED NATURE OF THE THREAT AND DECREASING INSTABILITY...WW ISSUANCE IS NOT ANTICIPATED BEYOND THE 09Z WW EXPIRATION TIME.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: THE LATEST WATER VAPOR IMAGERY SHOWS A WELL-DEFINED SHORTWAVE TROUGH IN THE OH VALLEY. LARGE-SCALE ASCENT AHEAD OF THIS FEATURE IS SUPPORTING A LINEAR MCS CURRENTLY LOCATED FROM CNTRL PA EXTENDING SWWD INTO NRN WV. THIS LINE IS FORECAST TO CONTINUE TO MOVE ACROSS THE CNTRL APPALACHIAN MTNS DURING THE OVERNIGHT PERIOD. THE AIRMASS AHEAD OF THE LINE IS STILL MODERATELY UNSTABLE ACCORDING TO OBJECTIVE ANALYSIS WITH MLCAPE ESTIMATED IN THE 1000 TO 2000 J/K RANGE IN SRN PA AND NRN MD. THIS COMBINED UNIDIRECTIONAL FLOW EVIDENT ON REGIONAL WSR-88D VWPS AND 50 KT OF 0-6 KM SHEAR...SHOULD SUPPORT A WIND DAMAGE THREAT WITH SMALL BOWS EMBEDDED IN THE LINE. HAIL MAY ALSO OCCUR WITH THE STRONGER UPDRAFTS. THE SEVERE THREAT MAY TEND TO BECOME MORE ISOLATED WITH TIME AS THE INSTABILITY DECREASES ACROSS THE REGION OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS. OTHER STORMS ARE CURRENTLY ONGOING IN AND TO THE SOUTHEAST OF WW 329 IN NRN MD TO NEAR THE DE STATE-LINE. THIS ACTIVITY MAY ALSO POSE A SEVERE WEATHER RISK WITH WIND DAMAGE POTENTIAL. DUE TO THE LIMITED SPATIAL THREAT AREA TO THE EAST OF WW 329...ADDITIONAL WW ISSUANCE IS NOT ANTICIPATED.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: OVERALL DAMAGING WIND RISK HAS SUBSIDED WITH W/E-ORIENTED LINE ACROSS E-CNTRL IND AND IS NOT ANTICIPATED TO INTENSIFY. LOCALIZED SEVERE HAIL/DAMAGING WIND RISK MAY EVOLVE OUT OF A CLUSTER OVER W-CNTRL OH. ADDITIONAL WW ISSUANCE IS NOT ANTICIPATED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: RADAR/SATELLITE TRENDS INDICATE W/E-ORIENTED LINE JUST E/SE OF INDIANAPOLIS HAS WEAKENED SUBSTANTIALLY OVER THE PAST HOUR. WITH AN OBSERVED WIND GUST OF ONLY 33 KT AT KIND AND MODEST DEEP-LAYER WINDS PARALLELING THE ORIENTATION OF THE LINE /PER KIND VWP DATA/...INTENSIFICATION OF THIS CLUSTER TO A SEVERE RISK APPEARS UNLIKELY. ANY LOCALIZED SEVERE RISK MAY EMANATE OUT OF A CLUSTER ACROSS W-CNTRL OH. 05Z SURFACE ANALYSIS PLACED A WEAK 1015 MB CYCLONE ALONG THE IND/OH BORDER WITH COMPOSITE OUTFLOW/EFFECTIVE FRONT EXTENDING E/SE INTO NRN WV. LOCALIZED DAMAGING WINDS AND PERHAPS MARGINAL HAIL MAY ACCOMPANY THIS CONVECTION...WHICH SHOULD LARGELY REMAIN JUST E OF ONGOING WW 331. ..GRAMS.. 06/19/2014 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: PRIMARY SEVERE RISK IN THE FORM OF WIND WILL EVOLVE WITH DEVELOPING MCV OVER CNTRL NEB WHICH SHOULD PROPAGATE E/NE THROUGH THE BULK OF WW 332. A MORE LOCALIZED RISK MAY DEVELOP OUT OF CONVECTION IN NE NEB ACROSS THE SIOUXLAND WHERE WW ISSUANCE IS POSSIBLE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: MCV HAS FORMED JUST NE OF LBF WITH AN INTENSE CLUSTERING OF STORMS LIKELY DEVELOPING E/NE AMIDST ENHANCED LOW-LEVEL SHEAR ON THE COOL SIDE OF THE SURFACE COLD FRONT EXTENDING FROM 25 E YKN TO 20 S BBW AS OF 06Z. THIS ACTIVITY WILL REMAIN CAPABLE OF SEVERE WIND AND MARGINAL HAIL. DOWNSTREAM CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT CONTINUES ALONG THE FRONT NEAR THE MO RIVER. WITH STRONG POTENTIAL BUOYANCY IN THE WARM SECTOR AND A 50 KT SWLY LLJ SAMPLED IN OAX VWP DATA...ISOLATED SEVERE HAIL/WIND IS PROBABLE WITH THESE STORMS. HOWEVER...MERIDIONAL DEEP-LAYER FLOW AOA 3 KM AGL THAT LACKS APPRECIABLE SPEED SHEAR SHOULD PRECLUDE A MORE ORGANIZED/ROBUST SEVERE RISK.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ANY LINGERING SEVERE RISK HAS LARGELY EVOLVED OUT OF WW 328 INTO 330...AND WW 328 IS EXPECTED TO EXPIRE AS SCHEDULED AT 07Z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: OVERALL SEVERE RISK HAS GENERALLY SUBSIDED WITH LACK OF COHERENT ORGANIZATIONAL STRUCTURES...EXCEPT FOR AN UPDRAFT ACROSS SIBLEY/MCLEOD COUNTIES WHICH LIKELY CONTAINS SEVERE HAIL. LOW-LEVEL WAA WILL PERSIST FOR THE NEXT SEVERAL HOURS ATOP CONVECTIVE OUTFLOW/EFFECTIVE WARM FRONT DOWNSTREAM OF THE 1005 MB SURFACE CYCLONE OVER E-CNTRL SD. WITH LOW-LEVEL SELYS TO 40 KT SAMPLED IN MPX VWP DATA...A RISK FOR BRIEF TORNADOES ALONG WITH LOCALIZED SEVERE WIND GUSTS SHOULD PERSIST FOR A FEW MORE HOURS /PRIMARILY ACROSS S-CNTRL MN/. GREATER RISK WILL REMAIN HEAVY RAIN WITH SLOW-MOVING/REGENERATIVE CORES. ..GRAMS.. 06/19/2014 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: RISK FOR STRONG TO ISOLATED SEVERE WINDS AND HAIL SHOULD BECOME INCREASINGLY MARGINAL.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: GREATEST NEAR-TERM SEVERE WIND RISK CONTINUES WITH MCS OVER CNTRL NEB /REF 57 KT GUST KODX 0748Z/...PRIMARILY JUST N OF EARLIER CONVECTIVE OUTFLOW/FRONT WHERE LOW-LEVEL SHEAR IS ENHANCED. HOWEVER...MID-LEVEL REFLECTIVITY HAS LARGELY WEAKENED AND CONVECTIVE OUTFLOW HAS SURGED WELL-AHEAD OF THE CORES. WITH MLCIN STRONGER WITH SRN EXTENT...THE MORE ROBUST COLD POOL WILL PROBABLY DECAY TO JUST ALONG THE REMNANT OUTFLOW/FRONT ACROSS NE NEB TOWARDS SIOUXLAND. IT/S POSSIBLE THAT UPDRAFTS COULD FLARE UP AS IT INTERCEPTS THE MORE BUOYANT AIR MASS OVER THE MID-MO VALLEY. A FLARE-UP MAY ALSO OCCUR OVER PARTS OF SE SD/SW MN AS W/E-ORIENTED CLUSTER NEAR FSD MERGES WITH OUTFLOW FROM DECAYING MCS OVER MN. ..GRAMS.. 06/19/2014 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...
